#5046. Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom: The AI Stock Winners and Losers After Jensen Huang’s Ousting

Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom: The AI Stock Winners and Losers After Jensen Huang’s Ousting

Wall Street is picking winners and losers from Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and the market is treating the chipmaker's competitors considerably better than companies tied to its business.

Nvidia shares fell 4.59% to $165.75 Thursday afternoon, recovering from an opening price of $151.01 and an intraday low of $148.80.

The rebound softened an initial collapse of more than 14%, but the stock remained firmly in negative territory.

The selloff followed Huang's immediate resignation as CEO, president, and board member after reports of extramarital affairs and allegations involving a suspected Chinese intelligence operative. Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO, although the company has not established that corporate secrets were compromised.

The stock was already in trouble before Huang stepped down. Nvidia had lost approximately $1.27 trillion in market capitalization between October 6 and November 6, raising questions about AI spending even before the leadership crisis intensified.

AMD climbed 5.79% to $584.89 after opening at $569.28, making it one of the clearest beneficiaries of Thursday's trading.

The company competes directly with Nvidia in AI accelerators, and uncertainty around Nvidia's leadership could make customers more interested in diversifying their chip suppliers.

Broadcom followed a similar trajectory, gaining 5.65% to $364.73 from an opening price of $356.80.

Unlike AMD, which competes through its own GPU products, Broadcom specializes in custom AI processors and networking technology, offering large customers a different way to reduce their dependence on Nvidia.

Google’s parent company Alphabet also advanced, rising 2.06% to $299.49 after opening at $293.77.

Those alternatives existed before Huang resigned, and Thursday's gains do not establish that Nvidia has lost customers. Investors may simply be pricing in better competitive opportunities if the leadership transition disrupts Nvidia's strategy or customer relationships.

Nvidia-backed CoreWeave suffered a much rougher session, falling 7.49% to $56.22 after opening at $50.91.

Its decline came just one day after the cloud provider surged 24.7% following quarterly revenue growth of 168%, so this may be just as much a correction after an explosive movement as it is a reaction to Huang’s ousting.

In any case, the relationship between the companies helps explain the anxiety among investors. Nvidia invested another $2 billion in CoreWeave in January and has an initial $6.3 billion agreement to purchase unused computing capacity through April 2032, making it an investor, supplier, and customer of the same company.

Any change in Nvidia's investment priorities could therefore affect CoreWeave beyond ordinary chip purchases, although neither company has announced changes to those agreements.

The pressure also reached the semiconductor supply chain. TSMC, which manufactures Nvidia's advanced processors, fell 1.15% to $408.61 after opening at $394.62, while memory supplier Micron lost 2.70%, trading at $789.43 after opening at $769.31.

SK Hynix, another major supplier of high-bandwidth memory used in AI hardware, declined 3% to $137.98 from an opening price of $134.25.

These companies depend on broader chip demand, however, so their losses cannot be attributed entirely to Nvidia's leadership problems.

For investors, the immediate concern is less about whether AI chips will stop selling and more about how Nvidia manages its partnerships, financing commitments, and product roadmap without the executive who built much of that network.

Nvidia's board has said it expects operations and customer commitments to continue without interruption. The company is scheduled to report quarterly earnings on November 17, with Kress now leading the business through its first earnings announcement since Huang's departure.

#5045. Bitcoin now looks cheap by one measure after $1 billion in ETF outflows

Bitcoin’s valuation signal looks cheaper, but five completed ETF sessions lost $1 billion. A durable recovery still needs buyers.

Bitcoin's latest on-chain valuation alert has arrived after five consecutive sessions of net redemptions from US spot exchange-traded funds, highlighting a lower valuation before the demand evidence confirms that buyers are absorbing supply.

CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost reported on Nov. 15 that Bitcoin's market-value-to-realized-value ratio, or MVRV, had fallen below 1.2. The ratio compares Bitcoin's market value with the value of coins at their last-moved prices. He called it the third trigger of his valuation preset during the 2026 bear market. Yet five completed ETF sessions through Nov. 13 recorded combined net outflows of $1 billion, according to Farside Investors.

The alert identifies a gap between lower valuation and returning demand. A lower aggregate valuation does not show whether new buying can absorb coins being moved at a loss.

CryptoSlate’s Bitcoin page showed $65,461 in a snapshot captured at 10:44 UTC on Nov. 15. The page said its price had refreshed about five minutes earlier.

MVRV divides market capitalization by realized capitalization, which values coins at the prices when they last moved. It compares today's aggregate market value with an on-chain cost proxy.

Darkfost identified earlier alerts in February, when Bitcoin had crossed $60,000, and June to July, when it reached $57,000. He also said the preset is adjusted over time to reflect MVRV's long-term decline.

That adjustment matters to the historical comparison. The post does not supply a threshold-change history or reproducible backtest showing what followed each signal. Three alerts within a bear market do not establish three durable bottoms.

CryptoQuant's methodology guide discusses MVRV below 1 as a possible-bottom region. That is distinct from Darkfost's adjusted sub-1.2 alert.

Unlike the specific holder-cost cluster examined in CryptoSlate's Nov. 14 coverage, MVRV covers Bitcoin's aggregate valuation. Both use last-movement information, which records historical positioning rather than current buying.

A separate CryptoQuant note from XWIN Japan, available on Nov. 15, cited a spent output profit ratio, or SOPR, near 0.98. The note did not identify the variant or exact observation time, limiting comparisons with other SOPR readings.

SOPR compares the aggregate dollar value of spent outputs when they move with their value when created. Below 1 means the measured outputs moved at an aggregate loss. It does not establish that every transfer was an exchange sale.

Adjusted SOPR excludes outputs younger than one hour, while long- and short-term-holder versions separate older and newer coins around a 155-day boundary. Those series need to remain distinct when assessing whether loss realization is easing.

Demand offers a separate test. Farside Investors recorded $185 million in net outflows from US spot Bitcoin ETFs on Nov. 13. That capped five consecutive sessions of net withdrawals from Nov. 9 through Nov. 13.

These are dated fund flows, not Sunday transactions, and ETFs represent only one channel of Bitcoin demand. Still, continuing redemptions leave that channel withdrawing capital rather than supplying the recurring inflows that would strengthen a recovery case.

Sustained improvement in a consistently defined SOPR series alongside recurring buying would be stronger evidence of absorption than a single valuation alert. Continued losses and repeated ETF redemptions would weaken that interpretation.

Pickleball shoes need to provide support, so buying the lightest shoe possible is not the smartest move. When buying a lightweight shoe (say, under 10 ounces) there's likely to be some sacrifice in support or stability. The trick? Stick to pickleball-specific shoes first. You can also consider tennis shoes and cross-trainers due to their similar support-first construction. Avoid featherlight running shoes that are built for a different type of movement.

Mesh is the most common and best material to look for in the upper of a pickleball shoe. However, like weight, you don't necessarily need the most breathable mesh possible. Some pickleball shoes sacrifice breathability to boost abrasion resistance, and to help keep your foot secure (like limiting your foot rolling and turning inside the shoe).

When it comes to the outsole, look for a shoe that has a strong rubber pattern that will help grip surfaces and reduce the odds of slipping when turning your feet. Some pickleball shoes pay greater attention to tread pattern, which can help provide a feeling of better grip on a court. When looking at the midsole, aim for a shoe that has supportive cushioning (like EVA foam) and keeps a relatively low profile. Prioritizing a midsole with too much cushioning could lead you to a shoe that sits high (like a Hoka running shoe), thus leading to a less responsive design, which could potentially lead to a greater chance of rolling an ankle when making fast turns on the court.

I have been fortunate enough to rock quite a few pairs of pickleball shoes over the past few years. If you're someone who's going to play pickleball once or twice for recreation, then you could get away with a low-profile running shoe. But if you're expecting to play any more than that, we strongly recommend buying a proper pair of pickleball shoes.

The reason we don't recommend wearing just any type of running shoe is that running shoes are made for forward motion, so there's often less emphasis on reinforcing the shoe for side-to-side movements. Running shoes also have less structure and stability than what you want in a pickleball shoe, as the running styles these days are made to be as lightweight and breathable as possible (with high cushioned stacks), which means less focus on overall support.

So, to be clear, you should steer from wearing running shoes for pickleball if you expect to play the game on a regular basis. A proper pickleball shoe is a smart investment that will help give you traction and stability while greatly decreasing the chance of rolling an ankle or spraining a knee.

#5043. Digital Credit: Comparing The Six Bitcoin Preferred Stocks

A simple four-part investor framework for evaluating Digital Credit.

Digital credit is an emerging asset class that transforms corporate Bitcoin balance sheets into income producing securities. Strategy pioneered the market with five perpetual preferred equity instruments: STRK, STRF, STRD, STRC, and STRE (the first four are listed in the U.S.). Strive subsequently introduced SATA and SATS, bringing the category to six U.S. instruments across two issuers.

These securities offer investors preferred equity (read: credit-like) exposure to companies whose balance sheets are dominated by Bitcoin. Their perpetual structure means investors principally rely on recurring dividends and the continued financial strength of the issuer. Unlike term debt, there is no maturation date at which the full principal is ever paid back.

Evaluating digital credit requires examining four characteristics: creditworthiness, investor protections, liquidity, and dividend profile.

This article explains all four dimensions and then offers a ranking for the six digital credit instruments along these lines. None of this should be taken as investment advice—it is only a systematic framework for analyzing digital credit.

Creditworthiness measures an issuer’s ability to support its financial obligations.

Traditional credit analysis focuses on earnings, free cash flow, and refinancing capacity. Companies with strong cash generation can service interest and repay maturing debt. Digital credit issuers today derive financial strength primarily from their Bitcoin reserves, placing greater emphasis on net asset coverage. In the future we could certainly see digital credit issuers that also have significant cash flows on top of Bitcoin holdings, which would add to creditworthiness.

The central question is how much Bitcoin supports each dollar of credit obligations. One useful measure is the BTC Rating, which compares the dollar value of Bitcoin reserves with the outstanding credit, accounting for the seniority of each credit instrument. Cash reserves can further strengthen creditworthiness by reducing net obligations.

For example, a 5x BTC Rating indicates five dollars of Bitcoin supporting every dollar of notional credit claims. Higher ratings provide greater protection against Bitcoin price declines.

Seniority matters because instruments from the same issuer can have different claims on the same asset base. A senior preferred instrument benefits from greater coverage than a junior preferred instrument: all senior claims are included in the BTC Rating calculation of a junior instrument.

Creditworthiness also depends on corporate governance and capital allocation. Management must preserve sufficient Bitcoin coverage while funding recurring dividends. Issuing additional credit increases dividend obligations, while assets accumulation (Bitcoin or cash) strengthen the asset base. Excessive leverage, poor treasury management, or sustained Bitcoin declines can weaken coverage over time.

Investors must therefore evaluate both their assumptions about Bitcoin’s long term performance and management’s ability to maintain a sustainable capital structure.

Investor protections determine what happens when an issuer fails to pay its promised dividends.

While creditworthiness concerns an issuer’s ability to pay, investor protections govern the consequences of missed payments, and more specifically the compensation investors may receive for delayed income.

The first distinction is cumulative versus noncumulative dividends. Cumulative dividends continue accumulating when payments are skipped, preserving the investor’s claim to unpaid distributions. Noncumulative dividends permit the issuer to permanently forgo a payment.

The second distinction is the treatment of unpaid dividends. Some instruments preserve unpaid amounts without additional compensation. Others compound arrears at the regular dividend rate. The strongest protections impose penalty rates, which cause unpaid dividends to compound at progressively higher rates as deferrals continue.

Penalty rates create financial incentives for management to maintain regular payments. They also compensate investors for the additional risk and delay associated with missed distributions.

Other investor protections may include restrictions on payments to junior shareholders, preferred shareholder voting rights or director elections, and dedicated dividend reserves.

These provisions establish the contractual guardrails surrounding dividend payments. Stronger protections increase the cost of deferral and improve the investor’s position to receive income.

Liquidity measures how easily investors can enter and exit positions without materially affecting market prices. This is especially important for digital credit, which does not mature and pay back principal on a fixed date. A liquid market is how an investor would “get his money back” if he wants to exit his position.

Digital credit has developed substantial secondary market liquidity, particularly in its leading instruments. The six U.S.-listed digital credit tickers are among the most actively traded preferred equity securities in the U.S. markets.

Two metrics help investors evaluate liquidity.

Absolute trading volume measures the total dollar value traded over a given period. Greater volume accommodates larger transactions and makes it easier for institutions to establish or liquidate positions.

Relative liquidity, or turnover, measures trading volume as a percentage of an instrument’s market capitalization. It captures how actively a security trades relative to its outstanding size.

For example, an instrument with $50 million in daily volume and a $1 billion market capitalization has 5% daily turnover. Another instrument trading $100 million daily with a $10 billion market capitalization has only 1% turnover. The second instrument offers greater absolute trading capacity, while the first experiences substantially greater trading activity relative to its size.

Absolute volume facilitates large transactions, while relative turnover reveals the level of trading activity relative to the capital outstanding.

Dividend profile describes the characteristics of the income an investor receives. Three main considerations are the dividend rate policy, payment frequency, and dividend yield.

The first distinction is between fixed and variable dividends. Fixed dividends establish a predetermined annual payment per share. Investors know the nominal income they are entitled to receive, allowing them to plan around a predictable cash flow stream. Variable dividends allow issuers to adjust the payout rate over time. These adjustments can respond to market interest rates, investor demand, or the trading price of the instrument. Fixed dividends prioritize income predictability for investors with reduced flexibility for issuers. Variable dividends provide flexibility for issuers but less predictability for investors.

The second consideration is payment frequency. Traditional preferred securities generally pay quarterly. Digital credit has introduced monthly, twice monthly, and daily dividend schedules. More frequent payments improve cash flow availability, accelerate reinvestment opportunities, and reduce the concentration of distributions around individual payment dates. After January 1 2027, all six instruments will be doing daily dividends.

The third consideration, and perhaps the most important out of anything mentioned in this article, is the raw dividend yield. This is the annualized income received divided by the trading price of the credit. A higher yield is generally preferred, but it also must be contextualized against risks and other considerations.

The following framework ranks the six instruments relative to one another. Rank 1 represents the strongest position and rank 6 the weakest, with ties where instruments share identical characteristics.

Creditworthiness and investor protections receive overall rankings. Liquidity is segmented into absolute trading volume and turnover. Dividend profile is segmented into rate certainty and yield. While each category’s segments can be evaluated together as a composite metric based on the investor’s own needs, I am choosing to segment them for more precision. I have also thrown out payment frequency since all six will be daily in less than two months.

For dividend rate certainty, fixed dividends rank ahead of variable dividends because their nominal payments are predetermined. This ranking specifically measures income predictability.

Equal signs indicate tied rankings. Liquidity rankings are based on average daily trading volumes from November 2–11, 2026, and turnover is calculated using the latest reported shares outstanding.

Creditworthiness: Strategy’s preferreds rank ahead of Strive’s because of their greater asset coverage. Within each issuer, seniority determines the ranking. STRF has the highest BTC Rating because it is Strategy’s most senior preferred, while SATS has the lowest coverage because it ranks below SATA in Strive’s capital structure.

Investor protections: SATA and STRF rank first and second because unpaid dividends compound at escalating penalty rates and holders can elect directors following prolonged dividend deferrals. SATA’s higher penalty rate ceiling and dividend reserve give it the edge. STRC and STRK both compound unpaid dividends at the regular dividend rate. I rank STRC ahead of STRK based on its higher current compounding rate, although STRK also gives holders the right to elect directors after prolonged dividend deferrals. SATS has cumulative dividends, but unpaid dividends do not compound. STRD ranks last because its dividends are noncumulative, meaning any skipped dividends are permanently forgone. Investors also have no right to bring on directors.

Of the six, STRC and SATA are variable rate instruments and the remaining four are fixed rate. This makes the dividend rate policy pretty straightforward.

The remaining columns—volume, turnover, and yield—are trackable numbers. For instance, here are turnover and volume numbers from the BFC Digital Credit Dashboard:

Each of the six digital credit instruments has a different set of tradeoffs. Investors who prioritize creditworthiness may prefer STRF, while those who prioritize dividend certainty and yield may prefer SATS.

The relative importance of each of these dimensions depends on the investor’s own needs. As digital credit continues to develop, investors can use this framework to evaluate new instruments and determine which ones are best suited to their objectives.

#5042. Who Is Colette Kress, Jensen Huang’s Successor as Nvidia CEO?

Who Is Colette Kress, Jensen Huang’s Successor as Nvidia CEO?

For the first time in 33 years, someone other than Jensen Huang is running Nvidia. And the person taking over is not an engineer, a chip designer, or a Silicon Valley founder.

Colette Kress, Nvidia's 59-year-old chief financial officer, was named interim CEO Thursday following Huang's abrupt resignation amid reports of extramarital affairs and allegations involving a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.

Kress will remain CFO while the board searches for a permanent replacement, according to Nvidia's regulatory filing. She inherits a company worth trillions of dollars, a shaken investor base, and a management structure built around one man.

Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013, when it was primarily known for graphics cards used in video games. She arrived with nearly 25 years of financial experience across some of America's largest technology companies.

She spent eight years at Texas Instruments before joining Microsoft in 1997. During her 13-year tenure there, she became CFO of the Server and Tools division, overseeing financial strategy for Microsoft's enterprise computing business.

In 2010, she moved to Cisco as senior vice president and CFO of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organization, managing financial planning and business development across the networking giant's operations.

Kress holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University, according to her official biography.

Her move to Nvidia came with an unusual endorsement. Her two sons, then enthusiastic gamers, encouraged her to join the company responsible for the graphics chips powering their favorite games, according to Forbes.

Huang personally recruited her, explaining his vision for AI computing on a whiteboard during their discussions, Wired reported. At the time, Nvidia was the smallest company Kress had worked for.

When Kress joined Nvidia, its annual revenue stood at approximately $4.13 billion. By fiscal 2026, that figure had reached $215.9 billion, an increase of more than 50 times.

Huang drove Nvidia's technological strategy, but Kress oversaw the finances supporting its expansion from gaming hardware into data centers and AI infrastructure.

Her tenure included Nvidia's $6.9 billion acquisition of networking specialist Mellanox and an increasingly aggressive strategy of investing in companies that purchase its computing hardware.

Those relationships now include CoreWeave, in which Nvidia invested another $2 billion in January. CoreWeave's rapid growth reflects enormous demand for Nvidia-powered computing, alongside the financial costs of building that infrastructure.

Kress also became Nvidia's principal financial voice to Wall Street, regularly explaining margins, chip demand and revenue forecasts during earnings calls.

Forbes ranked her among America's richest self-made women in 2026, with almost $750 million in Nvidia shares as of Wednesday's close.

Kress takes charge as Nvidia faces questions about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending. Nvidia had already lost approximately $1.27 trillion in market value from its October peak before the board publicly announced its investigation on Huang’s love affairs.

She must also navigate Washington's restrictions on advanced chip exports to China and scrutiny surrounding Nvidia's commercial relationships. The board has said it has no reason to believe company secrets or U.S. national security were compromised in the allegations involving Huang.

Her financial expertise cannot entirely replace Huang's technical background or his personal relationships with developers, customers, and governments. Maintaining Nvidia's engineering leadership will require close coordination with the executives responsible for its chips and software.

Kress has promised to build on Huang's legacy, saying that “Nvidia's strength has always come from its people.”

Her first major public test arrives Tuesday, November 17, when Nvidia reports its third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings. The company has scheduled its results for approximately 1:20 p.m. Pacific, followed by an investor call at 2 p.m.

#5041. How $10,000 in stablecoins would have gained €420 without earning interest

A fixed dollar-token balance would have gained 4.9% in euros from September 1 to November 13 before costs. A stronger euro can reverse that effect.

A dollar stablecoin can keep its peg while the euro spending value of a European saver’s balance moves sharply. At a perfect $1 peg, an unchanged holding would have gained about 4.9% in euros between September 1 and November 13, 2026, using European Central Bank reference rates and excluding costs.

The ECB’s household stablecoin analysis puts that currency exposure in context. Its experimental 2025 survey evidence identifies ownership of dollar tokens among euro area consumers. The subsequent exchange-rate comparison illustrates a separate point: stability against the dollar does not promise stability against the currency used to pay the rent.

The bulletin draws on Consumer Expectations Survey modules from August and November 2025 across the 11 largest euro area countries. In August, 5% of consumers reported stablecoin ownership by themselves or household members, while 13% reported crypto ownership.

Among respondents with crypto holdings, 17% reported USDT, 12% USDC and 10% the euro-denominated EURC. Those percentages measure how common ownership was among crypto-holding respondents. They reveal no token’s share of invested capital. Respondents could select several assets, and the crypto-holder subsample comprised 1,286 people.

The ownership observations date to 2025. The ECB flags small samples, questionnaire sensitivity and possible misreporting. It also says the survey does not directly report how assets were used, so the figures cannot establish payment adoption or tell us what households earned.

The two-date illustration takes September 1 as its chosen baseline. Different holding periods can produce different currency returns. The ECB’s dollar reference-rate history shows $1.1590 per euro on September 1 and $1.1052 on November 13, the latest working-day observation available for this comparison.

With fewer dollars needed to buy one euro, the same dollar balance translated into more euros. For 10,000 unchanged tokens worth exactly $1 each, the illustrative value rose from €8,628 to €9,048, a gain of about €420 before costs. Dividing 1.1590 by 1.1052 and subtracting one gives a 4.9% increase.

That entire illustrated gain comes from currency movement. Token quantity and dollar price are held constant, with no interest earned. Actual households’ returns would depend on their holdings, timing and costs. The ECB also publishes its rates for information and discourages transactional use, so retail conversion quotes can differ from these translation values.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Illustrative unchanged 10,000-token balance at a perfect $1 peg, using September 1 and November 13, 2026 ECB reference rates.

The assumed peg and unchanged token count hold the dollar value at $10,000 on both dates.

The November 13 rate translates the same dollars into about €420 more than the September 1 rate, before costs.

The euro value rises 4.87% in this chosen interval through currency translation alone, before costs.

Hypothetical unchanged balance and exact $1 peg, with no yield, fees, spreads or taxes. ECB rates are informational, not executable quotes. The chosen two-date window is not a household holding period or an estimate of survey respondents’ profits. No APY comparison or forecast.

Euro value = 10,000 / USD per EUR: 10,000/1.1590 = 8,628.127696; 10,000/1.1052 = 9,048.136084. Difference €420.008388; return 1.1590/1.1052-1 = 4.867897%. Values rounded to cents and return to 2 decimals. Bars start at zero on a common 0-10,000 scale within each currency; currency units differ between panels.

Hypothetical unchanged balance and exact $1 peg, with no yield, fees, spreads or taxes. ECB rates are informational, not executable quotes. The chosen two-date window is not a household holding period or an estimate of survey respondents’ profits. No APY comparison or forecast.

More generally, gross euro value equals token quantity multiplied by the token’s dollar price, divided by dollars per euro. Income can change the quantity or value of a position; a depeg changes the dollar price; exchange rates change its euro translation. Conversion costs reduce what is available to spend. A stronger euro can reverse the currency effect even if the dollar peg remains intact.

A separate stablecoin-yield study by DefiLlama Research, published November 12, examined a November 9 snapshot of 98 stablecoin pools with at least $50 million supplied, no token incentives over the preceding 30 days and a recorded 30-day base annual percentage yield (APY).

It reported a median base APY of 4.1%. Forty-eight pools exceeded the study’s 4.2% three-month Treasury benchmark, dated November 5; that selected group’s median was 5.4%.

These are annualized yield measures based on a trailing 30-day window. They cannot be compared as realized returns with the September-to-November currency gain. They do show why a quoted income rate gives only part of the euro holder’s picture. DefiLlama links higher premiums to additional credit, trading, liquidity or underlying-asset risks, alongside the risks of using smart contracts.

Bare token ownership is different again. Circle’s European Economic Area (EEA) USDC white paper says USDC itself generates no interest for holders and gives them no entitlement to reserve income. Earning a DeFi yield requires a separate position with its own terms and risks.

Redemption also needs a currency and an access route. Circle describes USDC as redeemable one-for-one for dollars. Although Circle Mint is institutional, eligible EEA retail holders have a separate route through Circle France under its MiCA redemption policy, subject to identity and transaction checks and an EEA bank account able to receive USD. Third-party bank conversion or incoming-payment fees may apply.

A holder saving for euro expenses therefore carries a currency exposure alongside peg and investment risks. Someone setting aside tokens for a dollar expense or offsetting a dollar liability may have a different net exposure. The relevant question is what the balance will buy in the currency the holder actually needs.

#5038. Tether wants its gold token to rival ETFs

New institutional trading and borrowing routes put Tether Gold closer to traditional finance, but access and cash-out terms still matter.

Anchorage Digital’s support for Tether Gold gives eligible institutional clients routes to sell or borrow against XAUT as Paolo Ardoino promotes it as a gold-ETF challenger. The competitive test is how readily those routes deliver funds at the size and price a holder needs.

In Tether’s November 12 announcement, its CEO said he believes XAUT is on track to become “the first true competitor to the gold ETF market.” A day earlier, Anchorage announced custody, principal-desk trading and collateral support for the gold-backed token. Like gold-trust shareholders, token holders still depend on counterparties to turn that exposure into funds.

Tether said KPMG U.S. audited issuer TG Commodities S.A. de C.V.’s financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025, issuing an unqualified opinion. The announced audit concerns that entity and year, rather than all current Tether reserves or today’s trading and financing terms.

For eligible clients, desk-sale proceeds come from the trading counterparty. Anchorage advertises USD or USDT borrowing against bank-custodied XAUT through arrangements with other clients. Borrowing preserves gold exposure but creates debt; the announcement does not establish bank-funded lending. It also specifies neither a universal sale settlement currency nor a fiat-withdrawal timetable.

Anchorage says it holds XAUT at Anchorage Digital Bank in the US or Anchorage Digital Singapore. The group’s footer names Anchorage Hold LLC as digital-asset trading provider, Anchorage Digital NY LLC for New York agency trading and A1 Ltd. as a principal-trading business. It does not identify one universal trade-contract entity.

Access is institutional, with limited high-net-worth availability and further requirements for certain trading. Custodied tokens lack Anchorage guarantees and FDIC or SIPC protection. Custody therefore provides neither an insured gold deposit nor assured liquidity.

Anchorage’s notice says US persons cannot purchase or redeem XAUT with TG Commodities. The issuer’s terms contain a qualification: US counterparties qualifying as eligible contract participants, a regulatory category, may be accepted at Tether Gold’s sole discretion. Direct purchases and redemptions also require verified issuer-customer status.

Platform eligibility, issuer eligibility and issuer acceptance are separate gates. Neither institutional access at Anchorage nor eligible-contract-participant status alone establishes the issuer’s acceptance. Anchorage’s notice addresses issuer transactions, rather than a blanket ban on permitted secondary trading or custody.

Even an eligible, verified issuer customer does not have an unconditional cash buyback. The terms describe whole-bar redemption for delivery in Switzerland. Instead of taking delivery, a customer can request that Tether Gold attempt a sale to a gold dealer or broker. Only a successful sale produces fiat proceeds, less fees; Tether Gold has no obligation to repurchase the tokens or bullion. That route also needs a buyer.

The iShares Gold Trust product page describes IAU shares trading on NYSE Arca through brokerage accounts. For an ordinary share sale, a market buyer supplies the money through the brokerage transaction. The trust is not paying the retail holder cash for redeeming a share.

Its currently linked prospectus, dated December 22, 2022, reserves creation and redemption of baskets to authorized participants, with gold exchanged for shares. Retail sale access and direct redemption access are different rights in this structure as well.

Borrowing without selling is also available within conventional brokerage arrangements, subject to approval. Fidelity’s margin FAQ lists ETFs held for at least 30 days as eligible collateral, with special security and account requirements, and says checkwriting, bank cards and bill payments can create or increase margin debt. That general policy establishes neither IAU-specific approval nor a particular borrowing limit.

Anchorage notice excludes US direct issuer transactions; issuer terms allow discretionarily accepted US ECPs after verification. Neither custody nor ECP status establishes issuer acceptance. Ardoino’s ETF challenge ultimately turns on usable access: a client who qualifies, a counterparty willing to transact and terms that deliver the funds required. Custody and collateral support create routes. Their availability at the needed size and price is the next test.

#5037. The 7 Best Head Shavers for Men in 2026, Tested by Grooming Experts

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Get the chrome dome of your dreams with these scalp shavers.

AS MEN, THE decision to go bald isn’t always one that’s made for us (thanks, genetics). But how you deal with hair loss is entirely in your hands. Sure, there are some viable hair loss treatments and shampoos for thinning hair that we certainly back. For many men, it's easier to just bite the bullet and shave their hair completely to offset any future thinning woes. If you are one of these men, more power to you! Hell, some men do it even if they’re not experiencing hair loss—and that’s cool, too. Investing in a quality head shaver will double down on the convenience factor of being bald by making the entire process seamless.

When you do choose to shave your head, the tools you use to do it are paramount. That’s where the best head shavers come in. These high-tech gadgets are specifically designed to make shaving your head easier, whether it’s through a multi-head ergonomic design or close-cutting technology (or both).

Far easier than heading to the barbershop every few days, these electric shavers are meant to be used at home. Think of them as an easier, safer, and quicker alternative to carefully taking a razor to your dome. But before investing in a shaver, there are a few key factors to keep in mind to ensure you select the absolute best one for you.

This tiny but powerful shaver is designed to give your scalp the closest shave possible, whether you prefer to do it dry, wet, or with the aid of other products. The five ScalpSafe shaving heads wrap around the curves of your head for a microscopically close shave, and the additional attachments, like a pre-shave exfoliation brush and precision trimmer, are nice bonuses.

Our editors also love that it pairs nicely with our favorite shaving creams and pre-shave oils, in case you want an even deeper cut. Its portable design makes it easy to carry in your luggage, though its travel case is sold separately. Not to mention, the five heads of this shaver definitely give an incredibly close shave—as close as the Remington and the Braun, both of which we found to be top of the heap in our testing process.

We also appreciate the additional attachments that this one comes with, unlike the Remington, particularly the pre-shave exfoliating brush, which not only helps give a closer shave, but also feels pretty damn good on your dome (you’ll want to only use this if you have a tiny bit of stubble though—the bristles aren’t long enough to reach through longer hair).

In theory, the trimmer attachment and the accompanying guards are great if you want to trim your beard (the brand also says you can use it to trim your body and other areas), but we found that the design of the device makes that difficult. Since it’s meant to be held in the palm of your hand, it’s not as easy to use on your face as a more traditional razor design like the Braun or even the Andis. We would probably skip that and relegate this device to only our heads, which, at a comparable price point to other models like the Remington, is OK.

Read More: How to Give Yourself a Buzzcut

If you’re in a rush, this easy-to-use shaver may be your answer. Thanks to the pivoting shaver heads that hug each curve of your head, the brand says that this device can shave your entire head in just two minutes.

After testing the Remington Balder Pro for over a year, we can safely say that it easily gave us a head shave in less than five minutes, which is great for guys who cut their dome weekly. We love the hair capture chamber, which collects hair for easy cleanup, and its non-slip grip gives you extra control when you're mowing through your head.

Keep in mind that this is designed only for head shaving, so if you’re looking for a more multi-purpose solution, you’ll want to go with a more traditional electric shaver like the Braun Series 9 Pro Plus. And since there aren’t any additional attachments like the kind that come with others, like the Freebird, you’re really only going to use this to give your head a smooth, clean shave (which it is frankly very good at doing).

The price is comparable to other head shavers, but we found that the performance outmatches them, so it’s a great investment if you’re a guy who shaves his head often and doesn’t mind having a separate tool just for that task.

If you’re not the smooth-shave type, but still want to give yourself a close buzz without heading to the barber, the Shortcut Pro delivers. With multiple length options via interchangeable combs, this shaver allows you to try different buzz looks on your own.

As the product image suggests, the Shortcut Pro is super compact, which makes it great for tossing in a Dopp kit and taking on trips. The feel of the shaver takes a second to get used to, but once you learn how to wield it, you'll find it does a solid job of staying cut-free while providing a solid shave.

It’s worth repeating that this won’t give you a close, clean shave, but it is handy if you like more of a stubble look. The design isn’t perfect and is less ergonomic than the Remington or one of the similarly designed shavers, but once you get the hang of it, it’s pretty foolproof.

Our one gripe is that because of the curved design, which is nice for hugging the shape of your head, it’s a bit difficult for detailed work around your ears or cleaning up your neck. A more traditional clipper is better for those things, but that’s a small price to pay for the convenience this one offers.

Like Braun’s previous versions, the Series 9 Pro+ has proven to be effective in performance. Not only is it one of our favorite head shavers, but it’s seen as the “Rolls-Royce of shaving instruments” by Faheem Alexander, barber and owner of Faheem's Hands of Precision in Philadelphia.“I highly recommend [it] because of the unparalleled ease and comfort it provides while also ensuring a super close shave,” he says. “The accompanying portable charging case makes this super easy to throw in a bag and get numerous weeks of shaves without plugging it in.”

During our trial run, we found out that the fast-speed device can cut up to 40,000 cuts per minute. Thanks to its waterproof capability, you can use it in the shower for a refreshing shaving experience. We also love that the device comes with a SmartCare center, which maintains the quality for longer use and makes cleaning up a breeze.

While this isn’t technically a head shaver in the way the two Remingtons or Freebird are, we found in our testing that it performs just as well at shaving your head as it does at shaving your face—it is our best electric razor.

What that means to us is that if you’re looking to streamline the number of devices you have in your arsenal, but don’t want to sacrifice power or efficacy, this is an ideal option. It’s expensive—as the Rolls-Royce of shaving instruments is expected to be—but if you’re using it for multiple things like shaving your head and face, that helps justify the cost a bit more.

Ever wonder how your barber gets such a close shave when he’s doing skin fades or cleaning up your neck? Enter this foil shaver, which is hard to beat when it comes to closeness. Not to mention, it’s a go-to for plenty of barbers. Speaking of which, Alexander gives the Andis tool his stamp of approval because it works efficiently for shaving experiences at home and in the barbershop.

It operates well on battery, delivering up to 80 minutes of run time on a single charge—a duration that’s twice as long as others on this list. The price point may be higher than most on this list, but the results make up for the difference.

This is definitely a classic for a reason—it really gets the job done with an incredibly smooth shave. However, it’s aggressive and not the gentlest experience, especially if you’re just beginning with it. Theoretically, you can use this on your face and other areas, too, but we found that the shaving experience is too harsh for us to use anywhere but our head and neck. You’ll also likely want to finish with some sort of lotion or moisturizer to minimize potential irritation.

Manscaped is one of the most consistent brands in men’s grooming, and this head shaver is a perfect example of why. It simply gets the basics right for a more enjoyable, less irritating shave. The grip, which invites palming, is super user-friendly, making moving the blades along your head easy with minimal effort (or risk of dropping it).

The brand’s signature SkinSafe blade guards make cuts and nicks rare, while the magnetic connection makes clean-up and replacements easy. With a 9,500 RPM motor, it shaves smoothly and efficiently. We found it also required minimal passes to get a full shave. Adding to its user-friendliness, the Dome Shaver Pro battery lasts up to 90 minutes and is USB-C chargeable. Plus, it’s waterproof and includes a sturdy hard-shell travel case.

This head shaver from the always reliable Philips Norelco is a great choice if you’re looking for a smooth, comfortable shave without the hassle. Its 360-degree flexing head follows the contours of your scalp, while the 36 self-sharpening ComfortCut blades deliver an even shave without putting unnecessary pressure on your skin.

The ergonomic grip makes it easy to maneuver, while the PowerAdapt Sensor automatically adjusts power to match hair density as you go. With up to 90 minutes of cordless use, water resistance, and a convenient travel case, it’s a reliable option for both everyday grooming and travel.

Most head shavers feature multiple razor heads to help hug the contours of your head so you can easily navigate areas that are hard to see. The multiple razor heads can also help limit cuts, as the design adjusts to curved angles much better than a single, straight razor.

For the quickest, most adaptable (read: lowest maintenance) shaving experience, look for devices with shaving heads in the five-to-seven range, like the Freebird FlexSeries or Remington Balder Pro. That being said, don’t fall into the common trap of thinking that more shaving heads automatically equals a more powerful shave, as the Braun Series 9 Pro Plus is one of the most powerful options on the market and only has four shaving blades.

Most head shavers on this list can be used dry, which means as long as your hair is already short enough (no more than a couple of days of growth), you can shave with no moisture or product. What's also great is that some options are waterproof, making your shaving experience in the shower a total breeze and easy to clean up.

Plus, you can use most wet/dry shavers with shaving products, so if you prefer to begin with a pre-shave oil to protect your scalp and then add a shaving cream or lotion to help with gliding. Follow it up by rinsing the product off your head—just make sure to also clean any leftover product from the razor heads before you put it away. However, there are a couple of options we recommend that do not have this capability, so if you’re a dedicated shower shaver, focus solely on the wet/dry devices.

A good cordless head shaver can last as long as 90 minutes, which means you can go a whole week without charging the battery. They also unlock the ability to shave in the shower or on the road without having to be plugged in. If you're constantly on the move and shave your head regularly, you will find that cordless options offer lots of convenience and save even more time.

Even before joining the bald brotherhood, most of us have all had an electric razor or beard trimmer die out before we've finished the job. Nobody wants to sport a half-trimmed beard or uneven body hair, but the absolute last spot you'll want an uneven shave is on your dome, as it's the hardest to hide.

To avoid walking around with a patchy skull, keep battery life in mind when choosing an electric shaver. Consider how long you typically take to shave your entire head—and how often you tend to charge devices—before finalizing your decision.

The first question to ask is: Does this shaver come with a case included? If yes, then you're going to want to look at what type of case it is. For frequent travelers, a carrying case made to fit neatly in a Dopp kit or luggage should be a priority. However, if you're just looking for something to store it in, you can allow for more size, given that it'll more easily hold every attachment or replacement piece, so there won't be any long search involved when needed.

For the past four years, Men's Health's grooming writers and editors have tested over 15 head shavers to determine the best-performing options for men. We also spoke with the barber and owner of Faheem’s Hands of Precision in Philadelphia, Faheem Alexander, who has put dozens of top-selling head shavers to the test and evaluated their effectiveness, durability, and ease of use.

In addition to all of this expertise and hands-on experience, we researched and dug into the top head shavers on the market to determine which to test. Following that extensive research and testing process, we landed on these seven best head shavers for men.

#5036. Bitcoin Price Briefly Crashes to $67,500, Lowest Since August, as Dollar Holds 19-Month High

Bitcoin price traded near $69,800 on Friday morning after briefly crashing to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern, its lowest level since mid-August, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The rebound held after October producer prices rose less than economists had expected, though the U.S. dollar remained near a 19-month high and traders still fully priced a December Federal Reserve rate hike.

Bitcoin price was trading near $72,800 at this time Thursday. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then gave way late at night, breaking below $70,000 and sliding to that midnight low. The move also pushed the bitcoin price below its 200-week moving average, a long-term trend line near $68,000. Buyers lifted it back above $69,000 before sunrise, and the rebound extended toward $69,800 after the producer-price report.

The U.S. Dollar Index held above 103 Friday after a three-day rally took it to its highest level since April 2025. The 10-year Treasury yield was near 5.15% ahead of the data, and two-year yields, which track Fed expectations most closely, were on pace for their worst week since 2024, Bloomberg reported.

Traders still see an 88% chance of a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting and a 12% chance of a half-point move, CME FedWatch data show. Fed Governor Christopher Waller has added a 50-basis-point increase to the discussion, and New York Fed President John Williams said Thursday that inflation remains high and policymakers need to take further action.

Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar tends to drain demand for risk assets. Both have pressured the bitcoin price since this week’s hotter-than-expected consumer price index.

Bitcoin has also broken from tech stocks. It fell 5.9% between Nov. 5 and Nov. 12 while the Nasdaq 100 gained 6.4%, a sign it is trading more on yields and the dollar than on the AI trade. Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 0.6% Friday after the producer-price report, as investors also weighed Nvidia’s announcement that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO.

The break below $70,000 set off a wave of forced selling. About $1.64 billion in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, with bets on higher prices making up nearly 89% of the total and bitcoin positions accounting for $916 million.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs added to the pressure. The funds posted about $47.7 million in net outflows Thursday, their sixth straight day of withdrawals, bringing the run to roughly $1.49 billion. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) alone bled about $2 billion over nine sessions through Wednesday, and the group has now flipped to about $1.56 billion in net outflows for 2026.

Sentiment has soured with it. A widely watched crypto fear and greed gauge dropped to 20 Friday, its lowest reading since July 8, and bitcoin is now on track for a second straight down year.

Positioning has turned defensive. Average perpetual futures funding rates turned negative for the first time in a month as the price fell toward $68,500, meaning short sellers are now paying to hold their bets. Order books are also thin. Bitcoin order-book depth across major exchanges fell to $72 million on Nov. 9, roughly 33% below normal levels. “Liquidity remains thin while leverage stays elevated, leaving the market vulnerable to sharp moves in either direction,” said Tanay Ved, a senior research associate at Talos.

The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% monthly increase economists had expected, after a revised 1.4% advance in September. Core prices, which exclude food and energy, increased 0.3%, matching forecasts. On an unadjusted basis, the headline index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler report took some pressure off the dollar, which still held above 103, but a December rate hike remains fully priced, leaving limited relief for the bitcoin price heading into the weekend.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $69,800.

#5034. Why the Path to Quantum Resistance Runs Uphill for Bitcoin Wallet Makers

Why the Path to Quantum Resistance Runs Uphill for Bitcoin Wallet Makers

Bitcoin custody has always involved some degree of risk, but wallet manufacturers like Trezor—which build physical devices designed to keep a user’s private keys secure offline—are preparing for a post-quantum world where new challenges arise.

That’s because SHRINCS, the community’s leading candidate for a post-quantum signature scheme, allows users to make transactions using stateful signatures that require rigid state tracking to prevent funds from being stolen, according to Trezor CTO Tomáš Sušánka.

Proposed late last year by Blockstream Research Director Jonas Nick and cryptographer Mikhail Kudinov, SHRINCS centers on a composite hash-based approach: users can make transactions using either stateful signatures or stateless signatures.

Stateless signatures are quite large—potentially affecting fees, signature speed, and other efficiency metrics—but are safe to reuse, while smaller, more efficient stateful signatures come with serious security risks when reused beyond a particular signing budget.

The stateful component of SHRINCS is made up of a tree of one-time signatures, and if these keys are accidentally used more than once, enough cryptographic information is revealed for someone else to forge that user’s signature and effectively steal funds.

If Bitcoin successfully adopts SHRINCS, maintaining a meticulous count of the wallet’s state will become a critical responsibility for wallet developers—with lots of potential edge-case security risks.

“You’re giving them an option to mess up,” Sušánka said during a recent episode of MARA Foundation TV, in reference to state tracking. “It’s our job to make it in a secure way, right? It shouldn't be the user’s job.”

To mitigate this risk, Trezor is weighing options for how to support secure UX in a post-quantum world. For instance, Sušánka said the company is considering making the heavier, slower stateless signatures the default setting for all users, tucking the riskier stateful option behind an advanced settings wall.

While Sušánka recognizes that SHRINCS may be the conservative cryptographic choice because it relies on the same cryptographic assumptions as SHA-256, he is “kind of torn on the topic because maintaining the state is a burden.”

“For example, you can have two Trezors with the same recovery seed. How do you share the state between those two? You really don’t,” he added.

“That being said, as it is with everything, this is about trade-offs,” Sušánka continued. “The [stateful] signatures are 10 times smaller ... That makes a big difference. So, I just don't want to throw it off the table completely.”

Sušánka went on to share that while many are focused on Bitcoin’s migration path to post-quantum addresses and signatures, hardware wallet devices will also need to be physically updated for full quantum protection. Most signing devices use quantum-vulnerable cryptography for hardware-specific security functions, like firmware and device authentication.

If users want to ensure their devices are secure in a post-quantum world, they will need to use “quantum-ready” devices—that is, devices that use post-quantum cryptography for device and firmware authentication as well.

In anticipation of these needs, the company is already shipping products like Trezor Safe 7 that support post-quantum cryptography for wallet authentication processes. Of course, transactions made on these devices will only be quantum-secure once Bitcoin itself upgrades to post-quantum security.

That said, Sušánka warned developers not to wait too long to give users migration options, as he believes the migration of potentially millions of users will take time.

“People should be ready to make compromises,” Sušánka said. “If we’re all going to be very strict on what can and cannot be done, we’re not going to get anywhere.”

A total of $798 million in crypto positions has been liquidated over the past four hours, including $718.5 million in long positions.

Bitcoin Bitcoin (BTC) and other major cryptocurrencies continued to fall during Asian morning trading as the fallout from Nvidia cofounder Jensen Huang's exit and expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike weighed on market sentiment.

The world's largest cryptocurrency plunged 7% over the past 24 hours to $68,408 as of 12:10 a.m. ET Friday, its lowest level since Aug. 20, according to The Block's bitcoin price page. Ether Ethereum (ETH) dropped 6% to trade at $1,921. BNB slid 6.3%, while XRP lost 3.5%.

Crypto liquidations totaled $1.47 billion over the past 24 hours, with 175,299 traders liquidated, according to CoinGlass data. Long positions accounted for $1.31 billion of the total. Notably, liquidations totaled $798 million over the past four hours, including $718.5 million in long positions.

"The sharp leg lower in crypto looks like a leverage event as BTC broke key levels," said Rick Maeda, head of markets at Laevitas. "BTC had already lost $72,000 in the U.S. session, and once it broke $70,000 late morning in Asia, the long positions clustered below that level were forced out quickly, with more than $600 million in four hours and over $1.3 billion in the past day."

The market downturn came as traders continued to assess the fallout from Nvidia's leadership shake-up amid expectations of another Fed interest rate hike, analysts said.

On Thursday morning, Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO after the company launched an investigation last weekend into his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. There had been reports that said Huang engaged in extramarital relationships with an Nvidia executive who reports directly to him and a second Nvidia employee.

"Traders trying to catch a reversal from the Nvidia-driven risk-off, combined with thin bids after this week's CPI, have both played a role in the liquidations," said Maeda.

Meanwhile, BTSE COO Jeff Mei told The Block that bitcoin also fell on assumptions that the Fed would raise rates in December to combat inflation. Mei said traders are watching out for signals of a potential 50-basis-point rate hike, which "hinges on how inflation and unemployment data will trend, as well as oil prices and geopolitical developments in the Middle East."

"If the Fed hikes rates by 50 basis points rather than the expected 25 basis points, bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies could have more room to fall," Mei added.

However, Jeff Ko, chief analyst at ViaBTC, said persistent inflation might actually strengthen bitcoin's appeal as an inflation hedge and bolster the currency debasement trade over the longer term.

"Looking ahead, markets will be closely watching the upcoming PCE in late November, and more importantly, the Dec. 9 FOMC dot plot. As for geopolitics, a de-escalation in Iran could offer one of the quickest paths to bringing inflation down," said Ko.

#5030. President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed

President Donald Trump sent the Senate four nominees for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Thursday, his first picks for either agency in about a year and the first Democrats he has put forward for them.

Former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson, a Democrat, and Republican Steven Levine were nominated to the SEC. Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland were nominated to the CFTC, Bloomberg Law reported.

Each nominee needs Senate confirmation. The Senate Banking Committee will handle the SEC picks, while the Senate Agriculture Committee will take up the CFTC pair before any vote by the full chamber.

Levine was tapped for the SEC seat left by Hester Peirce, whose term expired, for a term running through June 5, 2030. He most recently served as general counsel and a senior adviser at the White House Council of Economic Advisers and previously worked at the SEC as counsel and deputy chief of staff to Commissioner Mark Uyeda.

Peirce led the SEC’s Crypto Task Force and was one of the agency’s most vocal supporters of clearer crypto rules.

Johnson would take the seat formerly held by Democrat Caroline Crenshaw, for a term ending June 5, 2029. She served as a CFTC commissioner until 2025 and is a former law school professor. During her time at the CFTC, she spoke often about digital assets, including custody and decentralized finance.

Both CFTC nominees come from the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the derivatives regulator. Anonick is legislative counsel to Chairman John Boozman and was a lead negotiator on the committee’s portion of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031.

Rowland is a CFTC attorney detailed to the committee who also worked on the Clarity Act and the committee’s 2024 crypto bill. He previously served on Johnson’s staff at the CFTC, according to his LinkedIn profile. He would fill the remainder of former Commissioner Summer Mersinger’s term, which expires April 13, 2028.

Both agencies can seat up to five commissioners, with no more than three from one party. The SEC currently has two, Chairman Paul Atkins and Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Chairman Mike Selig is the CFTC’s only sitting commissioner.

The timing puts the nominees in front of a Senate in its lame-duck session, weeks after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, one of crypto’s sharpest critics, is expected to chair the Banking Committee when the new Congress is seated in January.

The pairing of Democrats with Republicans could matter for confirmation. After the election, TD Cowen’s Jaret Seiberg told clients he did not expect Democrats to confirm Trump nominees unless the president filled Democratic seats at agencies such as the SEC, a step he called unlikely. Thursday’s slate does exactly that at both regulators.

The nominations also land with crypto market structure legislation stalled. The Clarity Act failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15 and dies on Jan. 3 unless the lame-duck session revives it.

Without new law, the SEC and CFTC have set crypto policy largely on their own this year. Selig’s CFTC opened the door to equity perpetual futures, and a federal judge later said the agency likely overstepped while letting trading continue.

The White House did not say when it expects the Senate to act. The open question is whether a Senate heading for Democratic control moves the four nominees before January, or leaves the SEC and CFTC running with skeleton commissions into 2027.

The U.S. Department of Justice and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission have filed a lawsuit against Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin seeking to block the state's enforcement action against Kalshi, in an escalating legal fight surrounding the prediction market platform.

The federal agencies said that the event contracts targeted by Arkansas are swaps under the CEA, and that the state's efforts to prevent a CFTC-regulated platform from offering such financial products "intrude on the exclusive federal scheme."

The lawsuit comes after Griffin sued Kalshi on Nov. 4, alleging that Kalshi operated an illegal gambling platform allowing users to wager on the outcome of "just about anything."

The Arkansas AG suggested that such "gambling" on Kalshi is "squarely prohibited by Arkansas law."

The DOJ and CFTC are asking the court to grant preliminary and permanent injunctive relief, arguing that Arkansas law is preempted by federal law and can't be enforced against CFTC-regulated prediction market platforms.

The Block has reached out to Kalshi and Griffin's office for comment.

The Arkansas dispute comes amid a growing wave of legal challenges against prediction market platforms across the U.S.

Also on Thursday, Louisiana became the latest state to take on those platforms, with Attorney General Liz Murrill also filing a lawsuit against companies including Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood, and Coinbase.

"For too long, they have violated our laws with impunity. No longer: I am seeking an immediate restraining order and an injunction to restore the rule of law in Louisiana," Murrill said in a post on X.

Last week, a federal judge granted a preliminary injunction barring Kalshi from offering sports-event contracts on the lands of two California tribes — Blue Lake Rancheria and the Chicken Ranch Rancheria of Me-Wuk Indians.

A Kalshi spokesperson said the company had voluntarily withdrawn its services from the tribes' lands in September.

#5027. What to Know About Intermittent Fasting and Your Workouts

Yes, you can use this approach and keep training—if you have the right strategy.

DIETING CAN BECOME complicated, fast. Eat this, don't eat that, only eat so much of this, and eat even less of that. When counting, tracking, and planning all start becoming too much, many turn to intermittent fasting as an alternative. It worked for Los Angeles Lakers superstar (and Men's Health digital cover star) Luka Dončić this summer, too, as it was a key part of the overall training and nutrition plan. Doncic, who has occasionally had his conditioning called into question during his NBA career, seems primed for a big season this fall for the Lakers.

While intermittent fasting may help simplify your meal-prep routine, you might find that the practice complicates your workout schedule. The premise of the intermittent fasting diet is simple: only eat for a small amount of time during the day, and fast the rest. There are several different kinds of intermittent fasting schedules, but the most popular one requires you to fast for 16 hours, then fit your meals into the next eight. Whatever food you eat during that period is up to you, so long as you stick within your eating window (though, filling up those few hours with several cheeseburgers and buckets of fries probably won’t get you very far in the weight loss department).

Food fuels our body for activity, though—and when you take that fuel away for most of the day, your workouts will likely suffer. You may find yourself feeling weak and lethargic in the gym when sticking to a fasting schedule, which is not ideal if you’re trying to build muscle mass and keep yourself in shape. That doesn’t mean you can’t work out when you’re fasting; it’s more a matter of proceeding safely in a way that will still optimize your training. A few small changes in your schedule and practices and you can continue your quest for that dream physique safely.

Let’s back up for a moment. First, it's important to understand the intermittent fasting schedule before you consider how to implement the strategy within a workout plan.

The most common type of intermittent fasting is the daily, time-restricting format. Typically, there’s a 16-hour fast, followed by an eight hour eating window. For example, someone could make their eating period between 12 p.m. and 8 p.m., only consuming lunch and dinner.

The time schedule can vary depending on your day. If you’re a person that needs more fuel in the morning, you may run on a 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. schedule instead. The time of day doesn’t really matter, as long as the consumption window sits at eight hours.

If that sounds like something you’re interested in trying, talk to your doctor or a registered dietitian first. Fasting is not appropriate for those that are pregnant, have a history of an eating disorder, or have certain medical conditions—speaking to your doctor will ensure the practice is a healthy choice for you.

If you frequently succumb to the temptation of a nighttime walk to the fridge, IF might just be the thing you need to keep your snacking in check and lose that excess weight.

“Intermittent fasting puts a cap on eating and can eliminate or minimize overconsumption at night. This can decrease calorie intake, can help with better sleep as the stomach won't be having a fiesta when it is time for a siesta,” says Leslie Bonci, R.D., M.P.H, sports dietician for the Kansas City Chiefs.

Weight loss isn’t the only benefit to the practice, though. There’s some evidence to suggest that intermittent fasting can reduce the risk of diabetes, lower blood pressure, and help maintain muscle mass.

That said, intermittent fasting is by no means the perfect diet for everyone, or a magic bullet for weight loss. For some, it’s a simple practice that may help eliminate those extra trips to the fridge. But for others, eating in a small window of time is just not sustainable— and the best diet is always one that keeps you consistent.

If fasting is that diet for you, exercise is vital to keep your heart healthy and muscles strong while dieting. Take these tips to schedule your workouts appropriately with your feeding hours.

Whether it’s a 5/2 protocol (eat for five days, fast for two) a 16/8 (fast for 16 hours, eat for eight), or any other version of IF, most people on a fasting diet wind up losing weight. That’s because it’s much harder to overeat if all your daily calories are crammed into an eight-hour window than if you can spread them out over 15 to 16 hours. That’s what makes IF such an effective weight-loss tool: by restricting the time frame in which you can eat, you effectively restrict the number of calories you take in as well.

But if your main goal is maximizing muscle, fasting isn’t a great idea. “Unless you’re a real novice, you can’t build appreciable muscle in a caloric deficit,” says Angelo Poli, ISSA, co-owner of Whole Body Fitness in Chico, CA, creator of the MetPro diet and exercise app. A pound here and there? Maybe. But you won’t build anywhere near as much as you would if you consume a few hundred extra calories above and beyond what your body needs each day. So don’t try. Your primary goal while fasting should losing fat. To build muscle, you need fuel.

Even if your main goal is losing fat, you still need to lift, which prevents your body from burning through muscle to fuel your daily activities. You won’t gain much muscle if you’re fasting, but if you lift, you won’t lose it, either. “The same activities that build muscle when you’re fueled help preserve it when you’re in a caloric deficit,” says Poli.

Since you’re only trying to maintain the muscle you have—not pack on additional beef—you can get away with a fairly infrequent lifting schedule—2 to 3 times per week, exercising your whole body each workout (try this routine).

Lifting weights, sprinting, doing CrossFit WODS, and other high-intensity activities all depend on carbohydrates for fuel, explains Poli. If you perform any of these activities during (or worse, at the end of) your fast, your performance will suffer. Instead of getting stronger and faster, you may well get weaker and slower.What to do? “If you’re a big guy with a lot of weight to lose, no big deal,” says Poli. “Go ahead and lift on an empty stomach. You might lose a little bit of muscle, but you’ll burn fat, too—and that’s your main goal.”If you’re a slimmer guy worried about your muscle definition, no need to worry— we have a solution for you too.

It’s vital that you eat before you workout so that you can get the most out of your lift, but depending on your build, it might be good to ensure a little something afterwards. “Eliminating the post-workout refueling may delay recovery as well as muscle protein and muscle glycogen resynthesis,” says Bonci. So, if you’re on the slimmer side and are worried about losing some of your muscle definition, it’s probably better to schedule your lifting workouts during your feeding window. So if you eat from noon to 8 p.m. each day, try to hit the gym around 5, then go home and eat a high-protein meal to ensure adequate recovery from your workout. Bonci suggests sandwiching your workout into your meals if you’re limiting calories. Meaning, eat one third of your meal before the gym, and the other two thirds of the meal afterwards. That way, you get some in before to power the workout, and the rest after to recover. “Ideally, food and fluid would parenthesize the workout,” she says. Overall, it’s best to do your best to fit your workout into your eating period so that you can have something before and after. If your schedule just doesn’t allow for it, it might be time to adjust the structure of your eating period— either by extending it, or changing the start and end times. “The window of eating may need to be longer to accommodate physical activity,” says Bonci.

While fasted lifting is a big fat mistake, fasted cardio is fine—but know that fat burning and fat loss are not the same. This means your body is burning fat as an energy source—and, without a calorie deficit, those stores will be replenished. Fasted cardio is safer than fasted weight training, though—since your body uses fat stores for slow, steady-state cardio activities. For best results, schedule those lifting sessions during or after your feeding windows, and schedule cardio before them.

The key to exercising safety while using IF is to listen to your body. If you’re starting to feel light-headed after hopping onto the treadmill for some fasted cardio, be smart about the situation and stop and grab some food and water until you feel okay to start again. Carry a snack in your gym bag, for example, just in case.

To ensure you’re following a program that fits best to your body, speak with your doctor before starting up any new diet or workout program. They will be able to help you determine what will be safe and effective for you.

#5026. Strategy Made $19.5 Billion in Profit. So Why Is MSCI Removing It From Stock Indexes?

Strategy Made $19.5 Billion in Profit. So Why Is MSCI Removing It From Stock Indexes?

Strategy made $19.53 billion in profit last quarter. Yet MSCI, one of the world’s biggest providers of stock indexes, has decided Michael Saylor’s Bitcoin company no longer belongs in some of its major investment benchmarks.

MSCI’s November review lists “STRATEGY A”—the company’s MSTR shares—for deletion from the MSCI USA Index after trading closes November 30. That also removes the stock from broader indexes that include U.S. companies, such as the MSCI World and MSCI All Country World indexes.

That sounds technical, but the distinction matters: MSCI is not removing Strategy from the Nasdaq stock exchange, shutting down its business, or making it sell Bitcoin. It is taking MSTR out of stock lists that investment funds use to decide which companies to own.

Consider an ETF designed to copy the MSCI USA Index. When MSTR disappears from the list, the fund generally has to sell its shares, regardless of whether the fund manager likes Saylor’s strategy.

This is why it’s bad news for Strategy. It means less indirect exposition to investments.

MSCI adopted new rules in October for so-called non-operating companies. The idea is to keep investment vehicles—businesses that mainly hold financial assets—out of indexes meant to track operating companies. Its screening process considers a company’s operating assets and other financial measures.

MSCI’s deletion list does not spell out exactly which tests Strategy failed. The company, however, argues that raising capital, managing its Bitcoin treasury and issuing financial products amount to a genuine operating business.

In an August letter to MSCI, Strategy called the proposal “discriminatory, arbitrary, and misguided.” It argued that MSCI should be a “mirror of the market, not an arbiter of it.”

Strategy also maintains a software business, but Bitcoin now dominates its finances. The disagreement is whether its Bitcoin activity counts as running a company or mainly managing an investment portfolio.

Strategy’s latest quarterly earnings show $19.53 billion in net income. But that does not mean its software customers paid the company anything close to that amount.

Nearly all of its $20.91 billion in reported operating income came from a rise in the accounting value of its Bitcoin. Under rules adopted in 2025, changes in Bitcoin’s market price appear in Strategy’s earnings even when it has not sold the coins. A decline in Bitcoin can produce the opposite result.

Its software division, meanwhile, recorded $125.4 million in quarterly revenue, down 3% from a year earlier. Its $477.2 million in revenue for all of 2025 was slightly below the $486.3 million reported in 2019, before Strategy began buying Bitcoin.

The immediate risk is selling pressure on MSTR, not on Bitcoin itself. Strategy estimated that funds linked to MSCI indexes hold roughly 13 million of its shares, or 3.1% of its outstanding common stock. Not all of that necessarily translates into sudden sales, and Strategy says the amount is manageable.

But Strategy has repeatedly raised money by selling shares and other securities, then used those proceeds to buy Bitcoin. If its stock falls, selling the same number of new shares brings in less cash.

So the company would have to issue more shares to raise the same amount—or buy fewer Bitcoin.

That is why a stock-index decision could eventually matter to the crypto market. The exclusion does not force a Bitcoin sale, and it does not guarantee fewer purchases. It could, however, weaken a key source of funding for one of Bitcoin’s biggest corporate buyers.
